verdict: Avoid for now — lend only to established, cash-generating formulation units with clean receivables; skip new API/CRAMS capex and any borrower dependent on J&K local demand.
title: Jammu Pharmaceuticals & APIs: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
A pharma unit buys raw materials and intermediates, runs them through reactors and formulation lines, and sells to formulators, exporters or institutions on credit. **Cash sits in inventory and receivables, not in the plant** — rating reports show working-capital intensity of 47-52% for API players [10], so a unit's real risk is the gap between paying for inputs and collecting from buyers. Pricing power is thin for commodity APIs and strong only where the borrower holds a niche or a regulated-market approval.

## What has changed now
Jammu and Kashmir is visibly weaker than India: GST collections are -10.6% Apr-to-date against India +6.1% [D], and electricity demand is -0.5% against India +9.5% [D]. **Local demand and local activity are contracting while bank credit nationally runs at +21.6% YoY against output of -2.1% [D]** — money is chasing a shrinking base. Against that, the local pipeline is real: 29 units registered and ₹31.76 crore disbursed under a central scheme [2], and a ₹600-700 crore Orchid Pharma ACA facility is coming up in Kathua under PLI [3]. Note the Orchid project is a foundation-stone announcement, not a running plant.

## Where the growth is
Peer results are strong and recent: Aarti Pharmalabs posted record quarterly revenue of ₹613 crore, up 47% YoY, with EBITDA margin at 22.2% [4][6]; RPG Life Sciences grew Q2 FY27 revenue 16.5% to ₹211.6 crore and targets 25% API growth [7][5]. **Pursue established formulation units with domestic branded sales, and API units with a single validated product and export orders in hand.** Avoid greenfield API/CRAMS units, units whose sales depend on J&K government or institutional orders, and any borrower whose only collateral is land in an industrial estate.

## How to grow safely
Structure term debt short — five to seven years — and match working capital limits to the actual cycle, not to a projection. **Take stock and receivable statements every month, plus GST returns and bank statements**; if receivable days cross the borrower's own three-year average, ask for the ageing by buyer and stop enhancement. Where a customer contributes more than a third of sales, ask for the contract and a diversion-of-proceeds undertaking. For the Kathua supplier ecosystem, lend only against confirmed purchase orders from the anchor unit, not against the announcement [3].

## Early warning signs
- **GST turnover falling faster than the J&K state trend of -10.6% [D]** — pull the limit and ask for the sales register.
- **Inventory days rising while sales are flat** — this is the classic API trap [10]; ask for product-wise stock ageing.
- **Electricity bill or power consumption dropping at the unit** — cross-check against reported production; a plant running below capacity is burning cash.
- **Promoter taking unsecured loans from the unit or delaying statutory dues** — stop fresh disbursement and inspect the factory.
watch: turnover down more than 10% vs same month last year -> freeze limit enhancement and seek buyer-wise sales
receivable days above borrower's three-year average -> ask for ageing and stop new disbursement
consumption down while sales reported flat -> factory inspection before next renewal
statutory dues or salary delays -> escalate to credit head and review collateral
confirmed orders below 50% of projected sales -> convert term loan to need-based limit
